clue.text: Not a rank outsider

parts.note: a rank outsider is a no-hoper, but read literally this is someone who is inside the ranks of the peerage, a titled person

explanation.surface: A racing tipster insists their horse is no long shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank outsider' suggests a horse with no chance; here 'rank' means noble rank, and the person is no outsider to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer holds a title and so belongs to the aristocratic rank.

clue.text: Denying for example entry in a race

indicators.note: entry in indicates that the pieces make their way into the word for a people

parts.note: a nation is a race or people

explanation.surface: Someone refuses an example entry into a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' looks like a contest but means a people; 'entry in' puts the example abbreviation and A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusal or contradiction, saying no to something.

clue.text: His authority is brief

parts.note: a lawyer's authority to act comes from the brief, the case papers given him; brief also seems to mean short-lived

explanation.surface: A man's power lasts only a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' looks like an adjective meaning short; here it is the noun for a counsel's instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtroom advocate acts on instructions in a brief from a solicitor.

clue.text: Supply with goods a newly-wed — no?

indicators.note: newly signals these words are made into something new, rearranged

explanation.surface: A newly married couple are asked whether they've been given furnishings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly' rearranges WED and NO.
explanation.definitionFit: To provide with property, income or assets, as with a dowry.

clue.text: Dog under a log

parts.note: a firedog is a metal support set beneath logs in a hearth

explanation.surface: A dog is lying beneath a fallen tree trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The dog is a firedog, an iron stand for burning wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal bracket holding firewood in a fireplace, also called a firedog.

clue.text: Compensation — for radio silence?

definitions.meaning: something that balances or makes up for a loss
a wireless set switched off gives silence, read as two words

explanation.surface: Someone asks what payment they get for keeping the airwaves quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as two words: a radio with its set off.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount set against a loss to balance it is a counterbalance or recompense; and a receiver switched off makes no sound.

clue.text: Fraternity member calls for release of author

parts.note: to free is to release
A. E. W. Mason, the English novelist who wrote The Four Feathers

explanation.surface: A brotherhood member campaigns for a writer to be freed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calls for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the secret brotherhood of Freemasonry.

clue.text: In a way prison is barely enough

indicators.note: In indicates the jail goes inside the road abbreviation

parts.note: ST is street, a way
can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Somehow life in jail provides only just enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarcely sufficient, meagre.

clue.text: Appointments contribute to country's tsetse campaign

indicators.note: contribute to means the run of letters comes from those words, as a part of them

explanation.surface: Meetings help a nation's campaign against the tsetse fly.
explanation.walkthrough: Look in counTRY'S TSetse.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovers' secret meetings are dates or rendezvous.

clue.text: Does he do well? Might half do worse perhaps

indicators.note: half takes the first of the two letters of do
perhaps suggests these letters could be put in another order

explanation.surface: A man ponders whether he is thriving, or might be doing worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes D from DO, and 'perhaps' rearranges D plus WORSE. 'Does he do well?' means does he find wells.
explanation.definitionFit: A diviner searches for underground water with a rod, finding wells.

clue.text: Turn communist like the unsuccessful matador

definitions.meaning: to become a Red, read as two words
a bullfighter who fails gets pierced by the horns

explanation.surface: A bullfighter's career collapse ends in a political conversion.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming a Red is to switch politics leftward; a bull's horns wound the losing fighter.

clue.text: On which one maybe roamed in dry surroundings

indicators.note: the word dry forms surroundings, enclosing the shuffled letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of roamed could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A desert wanderer's mount is described as the beast one roamed upon across dry land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On which one' is the definition: the camel one rides on; 'maybe' scrambles the wandering word and 'surroundings' wraps the dry word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-humped camel is the animal a desert traveller rides upon.

clue.text: Telegrams concerning your excursion ? May send up mine

definitions.meaning: wires (telegrams) about a trip, read as two words
a taut wire that sets off an explosive when someone stumbles on it

explanation.surface: Holiday cables warn that the traveller might blow up their own mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'send up' means blow up; the mine is an explosive, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidden triggering wires detonate charges when touched; and telegrams were called wires.

clue.text: Music encountered outside pre-Christian books

indicators.note: outside signals that met goes around the books' abbreviation

parts.note: met means encountered
OT is the Old Testament, the scriptures before Christ

explanation.surface: A scholar met with music outside the old scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: A short choral composition is a piece of sacred music.

clue.text: It's able to fly or to land with no tail

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: with no tail asks for the last letter of the word land to be cut off

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something capable of flying may either do so or come down tail-less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no tail' docks LAND to LAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A small European bunting is a songbird, and birds fly.

clue.text: Airy quality of the dawn sky

definitions.text: Airy quality of the dawn sky

parts.words: Airy quality of the dawn sky
parts.note: airy can mean weightless or bright; the morning sky grows less dark

explanation.surface: A poetic description of the airy look of the sky at daybreak.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses meet: lack of weight (airy) and growing brightness at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of weighing little, or of being full of light.

clue.text: The Red Sea changing to green?

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of the sea's name are to be altered in order

explanation.surface: A geographic oddity: the Red Sea turning green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges REDSEA; 'The' is only a link. Reseda is also the plant mignonette, whose genus gives the colour name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mignonette's genus name also names a pale grey-green colour.

clue.text: Regular resort for trippers

parts.note: trippers sounds like day tourists going to a seaside resort, but these trip the light fantastic, dancers

explanation.surface: A seaside town frequented by day trippers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trippers' are dancers here, and 'resort' a place they visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A public venue where people go to dance.

clue.text: He's a post mixing drinks in these

indicators.note: mixing signals the letters of the phrase are blended together anew

explanation.surface: A postman is busy mixing drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixing' rearranges HESAPOST.
explanation.definitionFit: Small cafes are where people take cups of tea and refreshments.

clue.text: Shining example of a Victorian politician

definitions.meaning: John ..., a nineteenth-century Liberal statesman and free-trade campaigner

explanation.surface: A Victorian politician is held up as a shining example.
explanation.walkthrough: John Bright was a famous Victorian radical orator, ally of Cobden.
explanation.definitionFit: Luminous or radiant; and the surname of a well-known Victorian parliamentarian.

clue.text: Sluggish Oxford crew

definitions.meaning: a boat rowing in the ..., Oxford college bumping races

explanation.surface: An Oxford rowing eight is described as lethargic.
explanation.walkthrough: The Torpids are Oxford University's spring college rowing races.
explanation.definitionFit: Inactive and lethargic; and a crew in Oxford's Torpids races.

clue.text: Does such a company lose friends, Polonius?

definitions.text: Does such a company lose friends, Polonius?

parts.words: Does such a company lose friends, Polonius?
parts.note: Polonius in Hamlet warns that a loan oft loses both itself and friend, so a company that lends money would lose friends

explanation.surface: Someone asks Shakespeare's old counsellor whether a lending firm ends up friendless.
explanation.walkthrough: Polonius advises Laertes 'Neither a borrower nor a lender be, for loan oft loses both itself and friend.'
explanation.definitionFit: A firm that lends money is a credit or loan company.

clue.text: Three-quarters of this number being four

definitions.text: Three-quarters of this number being four

parts.words: Three-quarters of this number being four
parts.note: in a rugby union side, four players are called three-quarters; fractions seem meant

explanation.surface: An arithmetic puzzle about a number of which three quarters equals four.
explanation.walkthrough: A rugby union team has four three-quarter backs, so 'three-quarters' are players, not a fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby union team has that many players on the field.

clue.text: Account appears to be 50 per cent

parts.note: be from to be
half is fifty per cent

explanation.surface: A ledger looks to be exactly half done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears' is a link word. 'On account of' and 'on behalf of' share a sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sake or interest, as in acting on someone's account.

clue.text: Law that's obsolete, to be precise?

parts.note: ex means former or no longer current
an act is a statute, a law

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a defunct statute counts as precise.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate and correct in every detail.

clue.text: Going on a short distance

definitions.meaning: a single foot, read as two words

explanation.surface: Walking a little way.
explanation.definitionFit: Under way or in progress; and twelve inches is a small length.

clue.text: Radical progressives should excel at anagrams

definitions.meaning: people who re-form words, forming them again

explanation.surface: A claim that radical campaigners ought to be good at word puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as RE-FORMERS: people who form things anew, as anagram solvers do.
explanation.definitionFit: Campaigners seeking political change; and those who rearrange letters into new words.

clue.text: Arrange gems, or trees, differently

indicators.note: differently means the letters of trees are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: A jeweller arranges stones, or a gardener arranges trees, in a new way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' rearranges TREES.
explanation.definitionFit: To put precious stones into a new mounting.

clue.text: Previously an occasion for warning of course

parts.note: an gives the letter A
fore is the golfer's shout of warning on a golf course
time means an occasion

explanation.surface: In the past there was a moment for a golfer's shouted warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word, but it hides the sound of the golf cry.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word meaning formerly or in earlier days.

clue.text: Hat style has changed back all right

indicators.note: changed indicates the three letters of has get rearranged
back means the abbreviation for all right is read in reverse

parts.note: OK means all right

explanation.surface: A hat design has been reverted, and that's fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' turns HAS into SHA, and 'back' turns OK into KO.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall cylindrical military cap with a peak and plume.

clue.text: Thief's crazy about the adorable thing

indicators.note: crazy suggests the letters of the burglar's word are scrambled

parts.note: the word with its S, all six letters used

explanation.surface: A burglar is obsessed with some lovable object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges THIEFS; 'about' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An object revered or adored beyond reason, an idol.

clue.text: Establishes the choir where,?

definitions.meaning: the choir sits in the stalls of a church chancel, read as two words

explanation.surface: Someone sets things up and asks where the singers are seated.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as IN STALLS, the seats in a church chancel.
explanation.definitionFit: Puts in position or sets up officially; and the choir is seated in church stalls.
